library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

Maciel 2024 built two linked models for quinine given as the free drug or in
two lipid-core nanocapsules: NCP80 (poly(epsilon-caprolactone) coated with
polysorbate 80, anionic surface) and NCEUD (Eudragit RS100, cationic surface).

1. `Maciel_2024_quinine_rat` -- a two-compartment population PK model of
   quinine in **whole blood** of infected rats after a 20 mg/kg IV bolus.
2. `Maciel_2024_quinine_mouse` -- the rat PK translated to mice by allometry,
   driving a parasitemia model (logistic growth minus Emax killing) fitted to
   the Peters four-day suppressive test.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_rat"))$reference`
* Rat model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_rat"))$description`
* Mouse model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics16111369>
* Data source for both models: Michels 2019, <https://doi.org/10.2147/IJN.S227914>

# Population

**Rats.** Eighteen male Wistar rats infected with *P. berghei* received a
single 20 mg/kg quinine IV bolus on day 7 after infection, six per formulation
(free, NCP80, NCEUD). The whole-blood concentrations (197 observations,
0.083-24 h) were not measured: the authors multiplied the plasma concentrations
of Michels 2019 by in-vitro erythrocyte partition coefficients of 3.74 (free),
8.92 (NCP80) and 6.48 (NCEUD) (Methods 2.1-2.2, Results 3.1-3.2). Body weights
are not reported.

**Mice.** Four groups of five *P. berghei*-infected mice (free quinine, NCP80,
NCEUD, saline) were infected on day 0 and dosed 20 mg/kg twice daily
intraperitoneally from day 0.5 to day 3.5; 147 parasitemia readings were
modelled (Methods 2.1 and 2.4, Results 3.4). No quinine was measured in the
mice. The PD model was fitted against whole-blood profiles simulated from the
allometric PK (Figure 5).

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_rat")()$population)
str(readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_mouse")()$population)
```

| Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |

| Rat `lvc_free`, `lvc_nc` | 0.261, 0.028 L/kg | Table 1 (V1_pop, V1_NC) |

| Rat `propSd` | 0.436 | Table 1, proportional model 43.6 |

The rat column of Table 2 restates Table 1 as additive shifts, which the
packaged values reproduce:

```{r table2-rat-check}
t1 <- c(cl_free = 0.156, cl_nc = 0.059, vc_free = 0.261, vc_nc = 0.028,
        vp_free = 0.066, vp_ncp80 = 0.204, vp_nceud = 0.099)
t2_shift <- c(
  cl_nc = t1[["cl_free"]] - 0.0973, vc_nc = t1[["vc_free"]] - 0.233,
  vp_ncp80 = t1[["vp_free"]] + 0.138, vp_nceud = t1[["vp_free"]] + 0.0335
)
pct <- 100 * (t2_shift / t1[names(t2_shift)] - 1)
round(pct, 1)
# Each Table 2 shift lands within 1% of the Table 1 value (rounding only).
stopifnot(all(abs(pct) < 1))
```

# Rat whole-blood PK

## Virtual cohort and simulation

```{r rat-sim}
mod_rat <- readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_rat")

forms <- tibble::tibble(
  formulation = c("Free QN", "NCP80", "NCEUD"),
  FORM_QUININE_NCP80 = c(0, 1, 0),
  FORM_QUININE_NCEUD = c(0, 0, 1)
)

n_per_arm <- 100
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.083), seq(2.25, 24, by = 0.25),
                           seq(25, 96, by = 1))))

make_rat_arm <- function(i) {
  f <- forms[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose <- tibble::tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = 20, evid = 1, cmt = "central")
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      formulation = f$formulation,
      FORM_QUININE_NCP80 = f$FORM_QUININE_NCP80,
      FORM_QUININE_NCEUD = f$FORM_QUININE_NCEUD
    )
}
ev_rat <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(forms)), make_rat_arm)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_rat[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241125)
sim_rat <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_rat, events = ev_rat, keep = "formulation") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Figure 3a -- VPC by formulation

```{r rat-fig3}
sim_rat |>
  dplyr::filter(time > 0, time <= 25) |>
  dplyr::group_by(formulation, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10), Q50 = median(Cc), Q90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(formulation = factor(formulation, levels = forms$formulation)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~formulation) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Whole-blood quinine (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3a of Maciel 2024: median and 10th-90th percentiles."
  )
```

The simulated medians start near 100 mg/L for free quinine and 400-700 mg/L
for the nanocapsules and fall to about 1 mg/L by 8 h (free) and below 1 mg/L by
24 h (nanocapsules), as in the published VPC.

## PKNCA validation

The paper reports the mean whole-blood AUC0-inf of the data (Results 3.1).

```{r rat-pknca}
# The ODE solve undershoots zero by about atol in the far tail; assert that it
# is only noise, floor it, and drop the numerically-zero tail so the
# half-life fit does not follow integrator noise.
stopifnot(all(sim_rat$Cc >= -1e-6 * max(sim_rat$Cc, na.rm = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE))
conc_rat <- sim_rat |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(Cc, 0)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= time[which.max(Cc)] | Cc >= 1e-6 * max(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, formulation)
dose_rat <- ev_rat |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, formulation)

nca_rat <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_rat, Cc ~ time | formulation + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_rat, amt ~ time | formulation + id, route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
))

published_rat <- tibble::tribble(
  ~formulation, ~aucinf.obs,
  "Free QN",    127.8,
  "NCP80",      330.9,
  "NCEUD",      397.9
)

cmp_rat <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_rat,
  reference = published_rat,
  by = "formulation",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_rat, caption = "Simulated median vs. published mean whole-blood AUC0-inf. * differs by >20%.")
```

```{r rat-pknca-check}
auc_med <- as.data.frame(nca_rat) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  dplyr::group_by(formulation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(published_rat, by = "formulation") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * (auc / aucinf.obs - 1))
auc_med
# AUC = dose / CL, and CL carries only 8.5% CV, so the cohort median sits
# within a few percent of 20 / CL_typical = 128 (free) and 339 (either
# nanocapsule). The NCEUD data mean (397.9) is about 15% above that because
# Table 1 gives both nanocapsules the same clearance.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_med$pct) < 20))
```

# Mouse PK/PD

## Mouse PK at 25 g

The mouse weight is not reported. The vignette uses 0.025 kg, which the paper's
own numbers support: Maciel 2024 (Discussion) quotes a mouse whole-blood
AUC0-inf of 36.6 mg*h/L for free quinine at 80 mg/kg from Pussard 2003, the
data the allometry was fitted to, and the Table 2 clearance at 0.025 kg gives
80 / 2.19 = 36.6 mg*h/L.

```{r mouse-pknca}
mod_mouse <- readModelDb("Maciel_2024_quinine_mouse")
mod_mouse_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_mouse)

ev_pussard <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 80, evid = 1, cmt = "central"),
  tibble::tibble(id = 1L, time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 2, 0.05), seq(2.5, 72, 0.5)))),
                 amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 0.025, FORM_QUININE_NCP80 = 0, FORM_QUININE_NCEUD = 0,
                treatment = "Free QN 80 mg/kg")
# A one-subject solve returns no id column; PKNCA needs one.
sim_pussard <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse_typ, events = ev_pussard, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L)

nca_mouse <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(dplyr::filter(sim_pussard, !is.na(Cc)), Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dplyr::filter(ev_pussard, evid == 1), amt ~ time | treatment + id,
                   route = "intravascular"),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
cmp_mouse <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_mouse,
  reference = tibble::tibble(treatment = "Free QN 80 mg/kg", aucinf.obs = 36.6),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp_mouse, caption = "Typical mouse (25 g) whole-blood AUC0-inf vs. the Pussard 2003 value quoted by Maciel 2024.")

auc_pussard <- as.data.frame(nca_mouse)$PPORRES[as.data.frame(nca_mouse)$PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs"]
# Deterministic typical-value solve: only trapezoid and integrator error remain.
stopifnot(abs(auc_pussard / 36.6 - 1) < 0.03)
```

## Figure 5 -- simulated mouse dosing regimen

```{r mouse-regimen}
dose_times <- seq(12, 84, by = 12)   # day 0.5 to day 3.5, twice daily
pd_times <- sort(unique(round(c(seq(0, 320, by = 1), seq(12, 96, by = 0.1)), 1)))

mouse_arms <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c("Free QN", "NCP80", "NCEUD", "Control"),
  FORM_QUININE_NCP80 = c(0, 1, 0, 0),
  FORM_QUININE_NCEUD = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
  dosed = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

make_mouse_arm <- function(i, n) {
  a <- mouse_arms[i, ]
  ids <- (i - 1) * n + seq_len(n)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = pd_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "parasites")
  dose <- if (a$dosed) {
    tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = dose_times) |>
      dplyr::mutate(amt = 20, evid = 1, cmt = "central")
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      treatment = a$treatment, WT = 0.025,
      FORM_QUININE_NCP80 = a$FORM_QUININE_NCP80,
      FORM_QUININE_NCEUD = a$FORM_QUININE_NCEUD
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mouse_arms)), make_mouse_arm, n = 1))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = mouse_arms$treatment))

sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment != "Control", time >= 4, time <= 150) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 3.59, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.01, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Simulated whole-blood quinine (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Maciel 2024 (typical mouse, 25 g); dashed line = EC50."
  )
```

The peaks (about 4.4 mg/L for free quinine and 24 mg/L for both nanocapsules)
and troughs fall in the ranges of Figure 5 to within the weight sensitivity
described under Assumptions.

## Figure 6a -- parasitemia by group

```{r mouse-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241126)
ev_vpc <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(mouse_arms)), make_mouse_arm, n = 100)) |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1 | time %in% seq(0, 320, by = 4))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_vpc[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))

sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_mouse, events = ev_vpc, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = mouse_arms$treatment))

sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 24) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q10 = quantile(sim, 0.10), Q50 = median(sim), Q90 = quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q10, ymax = Q90), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Parasitemia (%)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 6a of Maciel 2024: median and 10th-90th percentiles of simulated observations."
  )
```

## Typical-value check against Figure 6a

The observed medians below were read from Figure 6a by the maintainers
(about +/-0.3 percentage points).

```{r mouse-fig6-check}
fig6 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~time, ~observed,
  "Control",   24, 2.5,
  "Control",   72, 3.6,
  "Control",  120, 4.9,
  "Control",  168, 6.0,
  "Control",  216, 7.4,
  "Free QN",   24, 2.1,
  "Free QN",   72, 2.1,
  "Free QN",  120, 2.6,
  "Free QN",  168, 3.8,
  "Free QN",  216, 5.0,
  "NCP80",     24, 2.0,
  "NCP80",     72, 2.0,
  "NCP80",    120, 2.5,
  "NCP80",    168, 3.7,
  "NCP80",    216, 5.0,
  "NCEUD",     24, 1.6,
  "NCEUD",     72, 1.0,
  "NCEUD",    120, 1.0,
  "NCEUD",    168, 1.5,
  "NCEUD",    216, 2.4
)
chk6 <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% fig6$time) |>
  dplyr::distinct(treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::transmute(treatment = as.character(treatment), time, typical = parasites) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig6, by = c("treatment", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = typical - observed)
knitr::kable(chk6, digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value parasitemia (%) vs. Figure 6a medians.")
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk6) == nrow(fig6),
  # Deterministic solve against a hand-digitised figure: the largest gap is
  # 0.43 percentage points; the digitising error is about 0.3.
  all(abs(chk6$diff) < 0.6),
  # NCEUD is the only arm that pushes parasitemia below its starting level
  # during treatment (Results 3.4).
  chk6$typical[chk6$treatment == "NCEUD" & chk6$time == 120] <
    chk6$typical[chk6$treatment == "Free QN" & chk6$time == 120] - 1
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Rat units.** Table 1 labels CL and Q "mL/h" and the volumes "mL". The
  values are per kg, in L/h/kg and L/kg, with the dose entered as 20 mg/kg:
  20 / 0.156 = 128 mg*h/L reproduces the reported free-quinine whole-blood
  AUC0-inf of 127.8 ug*h/mL, and 20 / 0.059 = 339 mg*h/L the nanocapsule
  values of 330.9 and 397.9.
- **Whole-blood data are derived.** The rat "whole-blood" concentrations are
  plasma concentrations times an in-vitro erythrocyte partition coefficient
  (Methods 2.2), so the model inherits the assumption that Kp is constant
  over time and concentration.
- **Rat IIV.** Each entry of the Table 1 IIV column is read as CV% with its
  RSE in brackets (for example CL "8.5 (32.4)"), the same "value (RSE)" layout
  as the estimate column. Exponential IIV, OMEGA = log(CV^2 + 1). The reverse
  reading (RSE first, CV in brackets: CL 32.4%, V1 120.1%, Q 30.0%, V2 29.3%)
  was considered. It is less consistent with the reported eta-shrinkage: the
  low shrinkage on Q (6.9%) and V2 (12.8%) needs the large Q and V2 variances
  of the adopted reading. Under the adopted reading the simulated 24 h medians
  for the nanocapsules (about 0.5 mg/L NCP80, 0.2 mg/L NCEUD) sit somewhat
  below the observed medians in Figure 3a (about 0.9 and 0.4 mg/L), and the
  NCEUD 10th percentile falls far below the plotted range by 24 h, because a
  small-V2 animal loses the slow phase entirely. Typical-value predictions do
  not depend on this choice.
- **Mouse Emax per formulation.** Table 3 lists Emax_pop, Emax_NCP80 and
  Emax_NCEUD. Results 3.4 describes them as formulation values ("from 0.055 to
  0.025 and 0.069"), and the maintainers checked the alternative reading
  (increments on 0.055): it drives NCP80 parasitemia to about 0.8% by 72 h,
  whereas Figure 6a shows it flat near 2%. The formulation-value reading
  reproduces every arm of Figure 6a (table above).
- **Mouse IIV.** Table 3 prints the Emax IIV as "0.008" in the CV% column with
  no RSE; it is taken as 0.008% CV (effectively none). Reading it as a variance
  of 0.008 (about 9% CV) changes the VPC only marginally. The EC50 IIV is 5.9%
  CV.
- **Mouse residual error.** Table 3 prints the additive error as -0.933 with
  unit "mg/L". The observation is percent parasitemia and a NONMEM SD estimated
  as a THETA enters squared, so the model uses an additive SD of 0.933
  percentage points.
- **Initial parasitemia (non-paper value).** The parasite count at infection
  (N0) is not reported in percent-parasitemia units. The maintainers
  digitised the saline-control median at the first reading (2.5% at 24 h,
  Figure 6a) and back-projected it to t = 0 through the reported logistic
  growth (kg = 0.012 1/h, Nmax = 9.2%), giving 2.0%. With that value the
  model also reproduces the control medians at 72-216 h.
- **Mouse weight (non-paper value).** No weight is reported; the vignette uses
  0.025 kg, the weight at which the Table 2 clearance reproduces the 36.6
  mg*h/L AUC the paper quotes for the Pussard 2003 mouse data. The allometry
  is steep (exponents -1.22 to -2.06) and the nanocapsule shifts are constants,
  so predictions are very weight-sensitive: at 0.026 kg the nanocapsule peaks
  are about 41 mg/L instead of 24, closer to the roughly 45 mg/L of Figure 5,
  and above 0.0276 kg the nanocapsule central volume becomes negative. Keep WT
  near 0.025 kg.
- **Mouse dosing.** Doses are intraperitoneal; with F = 1 assumed (Methods
  2.3) and no absorption rate reported, and Figure 5 showing instantaneous
  peaks, doses enter the central compartment directly. The regimen is seven
  doses at 12-84 h (day 0.5 to 3.5). Figure 5 also shows a non-zero
  concentration before the first dose, as if a dose had been given at t = 0;
  adding it changes the Figure 6a arms by at most 0.5 percentage points, and
  the protocol in the text is followed.
- **Mouse PK has no variability.** The PD was fitted against a simulated
  typical profile per formulation (Methods 2.4), so the mouse PK carries no
  IIV and no residual error; `Cc` is an output, not an endpoint.
- **Figure 5 troughs.** The simulated free-quinine trough (about 0.08 mg/L)
  is lower than in Figure 5 (about 0.2 mg/L); Figure 5 is drawn on a coarse
  time grid. Figure 4 (allometric fit to the Pussard data) is not reproduced:
  its concentration axis sits about 100-fold below the AUC the paper quotes
  for the same data.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (checked
  2026-10-31).
